name: MAX319ESA+T
title: Precision CMOS analog switches: SPST NC, SPST NO and SPDT
summary: MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319 are single CMOS analog switches with about 20 Ω on resistance: MAX317 is SPST normally closed, MAX318 SPST normally open, and MAX319 SPDT with one switch of each kind and break-before-make action. They run on ±4.5 V to ±20 V or a single +10 V to +30 V, pass signals from rail to rail, take TTL or CMOS logic through a separate VL supply and draw 0.0001 µA typical and 1 µA at most from each supply at +25 °C.
key_figures: MAX317 SPST NC; MAX318 SPST NO; MAX319 SPDT
20 Ω typ, 35 Ω max at 25 °C (±15 V, C/E grades); 40 Ω typ on +12 V

circuits.title: Figure 1: overvoltage protection with blocking diodes
circuits.description: A small-signal diode in series with each supply pin, anode toward the positive rail on V+ and cathode toward the negative rail on V-, keeps the switch safe when the supplies cannot be brought up in the right order. A signal source Vg drives NO; COM is the output. With the diodes in place the signal may reach only to within 1 V of either supply.
notes: The protection applies to MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319; V+ to V- stays within 44 V.

circuits.title: Figure 2: MAX317/MAX318 switching-time test circuit
circuits.description: The switch runs from +15 V and -15 V with VL at +5 V. COM is held at VCOM; the switched terminal drives RL = 300 Ω in parallel with CL = 35 pF. IN is pulsed from 0 V to +3 V with rise and fall under 20 ns. tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the logic edge to the output reaching 90% of its final level. CL includes the fixture and stray capacitance. For a switch of the opposite logic sense the logic waveform is inverted.

parts.note: 0 V to +3 V, tR and tF < 20 ns

notes: On MAX317 the output is taken from NC (pin 8).
VO = VCOM × RL / (RL + RON).

circuits.title: Figure 3: MAX319 transition time
circuits.description: MAX319 on +15 V and -15 V with VL at +5 V. NC and NO are held at opposite levels; COM drives RL = 1000 Ω in parallel with CL = 35 pF. IN is pulsed from 0 V to +3 V, edges under 20 ns. tTRANS runs from the 50% point of each logic edge to the output reaching 80% of its new level (0.8 VO1 or 0.8 VO2). CL includes the fixture and stray capacitance.

parts.note: 0 V to +3 V, tR and tF < 20 ns

circuits.title: Figure 4: MAX319 break-before-make test circuit
circuits.description: MAX319 on +15 V and -15 V with VL at +5 V. NC and NO are both tied to +10 V; COM drives RL = 300 Ω in parallel with CL = 35 pF. IN is pulsed from 0 V to +3 V. While neither throw conducts the output falls; tD is the time between the output passing 90% on the way down and 90% on the way back up, on each edge. CL includes the fixture and stray capacitance.

circuits.title: Figure 5: charge-injection test circuit
circuits.description: The switch on +15 V and -15 V with VL at +5 V. A source VGEN drives COM; the switched terminal is loaded by CL = 10 nF alone. IN is toggled by a +3 V logic pulse. The step ΔVO that the switching edge leaves on CL gives the injected charge, Q = ΔVO × CL. Which logic edge turns the switch on depends on the part.
notes: Applies to MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319; the output is NC or NO according to the part.

circuits.title: Figure 6: off-isolation test circuit
circuits.description: A 0 dBm signal generator drives COM through a coaxial lead; the open switch's NC or NO terminal goes by coax to an analyzer loaded with RL to ground. IN is set to 0 V or 2.4 V to hold the switch open. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V. The analyzer reads the signal that leaks through the open switch.
notes: Applies to MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319; the output is NC or NO according to the part.
The signal, output and logic leads are coaxial with grounded shields.

circuits.title: Figure 7: MAX319 crosstalk test circuit
circuits.description: A 0 dBm signal generator drives COM by coax; NC is terminated in 50 Ω to ground through coax; NO goes by coax to an analyzer loaded with RL. IN is set to 0 V or 2.4 V. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V. The analyzer reads the signal coupled from one switch into the other.
notes: The signal, logic, NC and NO leads are coaxial with grounded shields.

circuits.title: Figure 8: channel-off capacitance test circuit
circuits.description: With IN at 2.4 V the switch is held open. A 1 MHz capacitance meter, its other lead grounded, is connected in turn to COM and to the NC or NO terminal. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V.

parts.note: meter to COM or to NC/NO

notes: Applies to MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319; the terminal is NC or NO according to the part.

circuits.title: Figure 9: channel-on capacitance test circuit
circuits.description: With IN at 0 V the switch is closed. A 1 MHz capacitance meter measures from COM to ground, the NC or NO terminal left open. V+ (+15 V) and V- (-15 V) each have a capacitor C to ground; VL is +5 V.
notes: Applies to MAX317, MAX318 and MAX319; the terminal is NC or NO according to the part.

operation.text: Three monolithic CMOS analog switches in 8-pin packages. MAX317 is one SPST switch, closed at logic 0 (NC). MAX318 is one SPST switch, closed at logic 1 (NO). MAX319 is SPDT: COM goes to NC at logic 0 and to NO at logic 1, with break-before-make action.

On resistance under 35 Ω (20 Ω typ), matched within 2 Ω between channels and flat within 3 Ω over the signal range (bipolar supplies). Off leakage under 250 pA at +25 °C and under 6 nA at +85 °C. Turn-on under 175 ns, turn-off under 145 ns. Charge injection 10 pC max. Power consumption about 35 µW. ESD over ±2000 V by Method 3015.7. Maximum breakdown voltage is 44 V, and analog signals may run from rail to rail. The logic input is TTL and CMOS compatible.

Bipolar supplies of ±5 V to ±20 V, single supplies of +10 V to +30 V, and unbalanced pairs such as +24 V with -5 V all work; V+ to V- must stay within 44 V. Away from ±15 V the main cost is a narrower signal range; on resistance for ±5 V, ±10 V and ±15 V is in the typical curves. At ±5 V the switching times are at least doubled. On a single supply V- goes to 0 V; VL then goes to +5 V for TTL thresholds or to V+ for CMOS input levels.

Bring V+ up first, then VL, then V-, then the logic inputs. Where that order cannot be guaranteed, a small-signal diode in series with each of V+ and V- (Figure 1) protects the part. The diodes cut the signal range to 1 V inside each supply; on resistance and leakage stay as they were and the switch works as before.

Logic drive in the timing tests is 0 V to +3 V with edges under 20 ns. tON and tOFF (MAX317, MAX318) are from the 50% point of the logic edge to 90% of the final output. tTRANS (MAX319) is to 80% of the new output level. tD (MAX319) is the gap between the output's 90% points as one throw opens and the other closes, both throws tied to +10 V.
C grade 0 °C to +70 °C; E grade -40 °C to +85 °C; M grade -55 °C to +125 °C in CERDIP only. Each part comes in 8-pin plastic DIP, SO and CERDIP, and as dice in C grade.
32 transistors on a 0.058 in × 0.076 in (1.47 mm × 1.93 mm) die; the substrate is tied to V+. A silicon-gate CMOS process.
